explain.say: What is a turning point? It is a moment when the story changes direction, like a goal that flips a football match. World War Two, from 1939 to 1945, had several. This timeline shows the biggest ones. Let's look.

faq.q: Why was the Battle of Britain important?
faq.a: In 1940 Germany needed control of the air to invade Britain. The Royal Air Force, with many pilots from Poland, Czechoslovakia, the Commonwealth and elsewhere, defeated the German air force, so the invasion was called off.
asks: What happened in the Battle of Britain?

faq.q: Why did Japan attack Pearl Harbor?
faq.a: Japan wanted to knock out the US Pacific Fleet so it could expand in Asia and the Pacific, after the US cut off its oil supplies. The attack on 7 December 1941 brought the USA into the war.

faq.q: Why was Stalingrad a turning point?
faq.a: From August 1942 to February 1943, Soviet forces defended the city and then surrounded the German Sixth Army, which surrendered. Germany never recovered its strength in the east.
On 6 June 1944, about 156,000 Allied troops from the USA, Britain, Canada and other countries landed on the beaches of Normandy in France. It opened a western front that helped free Western Europe.

faq.q: Why were atomic bombs dropped on Japan?
faq.a: The US dropped them on Hiroshima on 6 August and Nagasaki on 9 August 1945, aiming to force Japan to surrender without an invasion. Well over 100,000 people were killed. Whether it was necessary is still strongly debated.

facts: D-Day, the Normandy landings, took place on 6 June 1944.
The German Sixth Army surrendered at Stalingrad in February 1943.

quiz.why: Allied troops landed on the beaches of Normandy on 6 June 1944.
